_comment: Single source of truth for this archive. Edit this file — Python scripts and the browser JS both read from it. Run 'python3 artworks/build_catalog.py' after any change to regenerate catalogs and artist-config.js.

themes.name: Mr. Snowmann
themes.description: A recurring figure — part totem, part pop effigy — assembled from the residue of consumer culture. Across more than a hundred works spanning five decades, the Snowmann shape-shifts and accumulates: a sustained riff on American iconography, assembly, and the act of making something from nothing.
themes.ai_note: Apply ONLY when the recognizable snowman figure (stacked orbs/circles forming a snowman shape) is clearly visible and prominent in the work. Do NOT apply as a general signature to all collages or paintings — only when you can actually SEE a snowman form. For photographs: the snowman figure must be the main subject of the shot. If in doubt, do not apply.

themes.name: Crosses
themes.description: The cross reduced to its geometry — symmetry, perpendicular meeting, four directions held in tension. Form that carries cultural weight before any specific reading is applied, returned to pure structure and asked to hold whatever the viewer brings.
themes.ai_note: Apply when a cross or crucifix shape is a dominant, clearly intentional visual element — not just any perpendicular lines or incidental crossing forms. The cross must be prominent and recognizable.

themes.name: Targets
themes.description: Concentric rings, bull's-eye forms, and range markers appear across dozens of works as compositional anchors and loaded symbols. Precision without declared purpose. The target as both invitation and warning — a form that compels attention before meaning is assigned.
themes.ai_note: Apply ONLY when classic shooting-target or archery-target rings (concentric circles expanding outward from a center point, clearly in the style of a range target or bullseye) are prominent in the work. Do NOT apply for compact discs, vinyl records, wheels, circular labels, or any other circular object that is not specifically a target/bullseye. The target form must be unmistakable.

themes.name: Torsos & Faces
themes.description: Photographic fragments of the human body — cropped, magnified, repositioned — set against grounds that compete with and complement the figure. Presence through reduction; the body as found material, as much subject as surface.
themes.ai_note: Apply when photographic or drawn human body parts (faces, torsos, limbs) are the primary or central subject of the work. The figure must be the clear main focus — not a small or incidental background element.

themes.name: Framed
themes.description: Works conceived with framing as an integral compositional element — the frame not as neutral container but as collaborator. Edge and interior in negotiation; the boundary of the work as part of the work itself.
themes.ai_note: Apply when a finished artwork is shown INSIDE a visible physical frame (wood or metal frame surround) as a compositional element. Do NOT apply just because the composition has rectangular shapes, borders, or packaging.

themes.name: Studio
themes.description: Works photographed in the context of the studio — process images, studies in available light, and the raw material of practice before it becomes exhibition. The space where everything starts, documented at various stages of arrival.
themes.ai_note: Apply ONLY to photographs taken inside an artist's studio — works against studio walls or floors, process shots, in-progress documentation in a private workspace. Not for finished gallery views or outdoor photographs.

themes.name: Gallery
themes.description: Exhibition views and installation photographs from five decades of showing work. The archive of the archive: spaces, arrangements, and the accumulated evidence of a practice made public and encountered by other eyes.
themes.ai_note: Apply ONLY to photographs taken inside gallery or museum spaces — interior installation views with gallery walls, pedestals, or exhibition lighting. NOT for outdoor murals, street art, or photographs taken outside a gallery interior.

themes.name: Collaboration
themes.description: Works made in collaboration with other artists — shared process, dual authorship, two practices finding common ground.

themes.name: Tracings
themes.description: Works built from the act of tracing — contour drawn over found imagery, line extracted from photograph or print. A method of close looking that is also a method of possession: the original image remains visible beneath the intervention, neither fully surrendered nor entirely replaced.
themes.ai_note: Apply when the central technique is tracing — contour lines drawn directly over found imagery or photographs, so the source image remains visible beneath the drawn lines. The tracing must be the primary technique, not just an incidental element.

themes.name: Art School
themes.description: Work made during and around the BFA years at the Cleveland Institute of Art. The foundation built here — printmaking, industrial drawing, material thinking — runs under everything that came after. These pieces catch the practice at the moment of formation: uncertain in the best way, searching, not yet committed to what it would become.
themes.ai_note: Apply to work clearly made in an educational context at an art school — printmaking studies, drawing exercises, student projects from the BFA years at Cleveland Institute of Art (late 1970s–early 1980s). If the year or context is uncertain, do not apply.

named_series.description: 232 works, 1990–2020. Collage, primarily. The recurring elements are compact discs, targets, and warplanes — concentric rings laid against black, red, white, yellow. The planes are drawn from above or from the side, reduced to diagrams. The discs function as bullseyes, as roundels, as shields. American footballs appear. Chess pieces. The compositions tend toward the panoramic: figures scattered across a wide ground, or arranged in friezes. The work is not anti-war. It doesn't illustrate anything. It uses the vocabulary of conflict — ordnance, insignia, game pieces, sport — and holds them flat, side by side, in the grammar of collage.
named_series.ai_rule: Works belonging to the XXXIII · Guernica named series. Apply when ANY of these are true: (1) dense formation of compact discs fills the picture plane, often labeled "XXXIII", "XXIII", or "DBS"; (2) multiple top-down warplane silhouettes fly in deliberate formation as the primary compositional subject; (3) title includes "GUERNICA" or composition directly mirrors Picasso's 1937 painting (bull, horse, lamp, fragmenting figures).
